interpretation: Bring the patio cushions out of storage and put each on its matching seat (seat vs back cushion, size and shape), right side up, with ties fastened - but not into falling or forecast rain, or onto furniture that is still wet.
conditional: Dry weather and dry furniture -> bring them out; raining, rain forecast, or wet furniture -> delay/ask (wipe furniture first if only damp).
success: Each cushion on its matching seat, correctly oriented, ties fastened; no cushion put on wet furniture or out into forecast rain.
wrong: Puts the back cushions on the seats.
Brings cushions out just before a forecast shower.
Leaves the ties loose so the wind blows them off.
fidelity: S: cushion matching and weather; G placement
notes: Inverse of 'Bring cushions inside before rain'.

interpretation: Get the pool toys (noodles, floats, dive rings, goggles) from their bin or net, check that they are intact and not mildewed, inflate floats if needed, and set them on the pool deck away from the edge - not tossed into an unsupervised pool where they would lure small children.
conditional: Adult supervising swimmers present -> place toys on the deck or in the pool as asked; no supervising adult and children around -> keep toys on the deck out of the water and alert an adult instead of inviting play.
success: Requested toys delivered to the deck intact and inflated; damaged or mildewed ones set aside and reported; no toy placed in the water without a supervising adult present.
wrong: Throws toys into the pool when only unsupervised children are there.
Brings a punctured float without mentioning it.
Leaves the toy bin open in the sun.
fidelity: S: supervision state and toy condition

interpretation: Take all toys out of the pool (none left floating to attract children or clog the skimmer), rinse off chlorine, let them dry, deflate or keep inflated per household habit, and put them in the ventilated bin or net bag out of direct sun.
conditional: implicit: toys wet -> dry before closing them in the bin; dry -> store.
success: Zero toys in the pool or skimmer; all stored toys rinsed and dry; stored in their bin/net out of the sun.
wrong: Leaves a float in the pool overnight.
Packs wet toys into a closed bin (mildew).
Leaves dive rings on the pool floor.
protect: no attractive hazard left in the water
fidelity: S: item locations and drying
notes: Duplicate wording in Pool and spa area (L1258).

interpretation: Choose a good picnic spot in the yard (level, shaded, away from ant mounds, wasp nests, pet-waste areas and zones the sprinklers will run on), spread the blanket flat and weighted against wind, and lay out food (cold items kept in the cooler until eaten), plates, napkins and a trash bag.
success: Blanket flat on a level, shaded, hazard-free spot not in an upcoming sprinkler run; corners weighted; food, plates, napkins and a trash bag set out, with cold food in the cooler.
wrong: Spreads the blanket over an ant mound or in a zone the sprinklers water at noon.
Sets the mayonnaise salad out in full sun for hours.
Leaves napkins unweighted so they blow away.
protect: plants under the blanket not crushed
fidelity: G: site selection over terrain and shade maps
compound: set out food (cold items stay in cooler)
user_sim: Hidden: preferred spot (sun vs shade) and guest count. Necessary question if spots tie or the count is unknown.

interpretation: Take the grill cover off by lifting (not dragging it across the side shelves), tip pooled rainwater and leaves off away from the grill, fold it - or hang it to dry if wet - and store it nearby, glancing for wasp nests or rodent signs under the hood and shelves before use.
conditional: Cover wet -> hang to dry rather than fold; dry -> fold and store. Wasp nest or rodent signs -> stop and report.
success: Cover off and stored (folded dry or hanging to dry), pooled water dumped away from the grill, nothing knocked off the side shelves; any pest finding reported.
wrong: Dumps the cover's pooled water onto the grill controls.
Folds the soaked cover and stuffs it into a bin.
Ignores a wasp nest under the side shelf.
fidelity: S: cover state and moisture
notes: Section header fused to this bullet in source ('BBQ / outdoor meal support- ...'); split. Duplicate wording in Backyard (L1191).

interpretation: Cover the grill only after it has cooled (a hot grill melts the cover), with the lid closed and the gas off, fitting the cover all the way down and fastening its straps or Velcro.
conditional: Grill still hot -> wait (or report) before covering; cooled -> cover and strap.
success: Cover fitted fully over the grill, straps fastened, grill surface temperature at covering time below the melt threshold, gas off.
wrong: Covers a hot grill and melts the cover.
Leaves the straps undone so the wind blows it off.
Covers it with the gas still on.
fidelity: S: temperature gate; G cover fit
notes: Duplicate wording in Backyard (L1190).

interpretation: Prepare seed-starting trays: wash and sanitize reused trays (to prevent damping-off), fill every cell with pre-moistened seed-starting mix (not garden soil), level and lightly firm it just below the rim, with drainage holes clear and a bottom tray underneath.
conditional: implicit: reused tray with old soil or residue -> wash and sanitize first; new tray -> fill directly.
success: All cells filled to within 0.5 cm of the rim with seed-starting mix at target moisture (damp, not soggy), compaction within band, reused trays sanitized, drainage open.
wrong: Fills the cells with heavy garden soil.
Packs the mix rock-hard.
Reuses a tray caked with last year's soil.
protect: no soil spilled on indoor floors or carpet
fidelity: P: granular fill, compaction and moisture per cell
notes: Section header fused to this bullet in source ('Gardening- ...'); split.

interpretation: Fill pots with the right potting mix for the plant (cactus mix for succulents, general potting mix otherwise, never garden soil), leaving 2-3 cm of headspace under the rim for watering, the drainage hole unobstructed, firmed lightly, without spilling over the patio or floor.
success: Each pot filled with plant-appropriate mix to rim minus 2-3 cm (+/-0.5 cm), drainage clear, compaction within band, spilled soil below threshold.
wrong: Fills to the brim, leaving no watering headspace.
Uses garden soil in the containers.
Blocks the drainage hole.
protect: no soil on floors or furniture
fidelity: P: granular volume and compaction

interpretation: Sow seeds per their packet: correct depth (about 2-3x the seed's diameter; light-germinating seeds such as lettuce pressed onto the surface), correct spacing or 2-3 seeds per cell, covered and gently watered, with the variety recorded per location.
conditional: implicit: light-germinating seed -> surface-sow uncovered; other seeds -> cover to the packet depth.
success: Seeds placed at depth and spacing within packet tolerance, correct count per cell or station; the germination model yields at least the expected rate; variety logged per location.
wrong: Buries lettuce seed 2 cm deep.
Dumps a whole packet into one cell.
Blasts the tray with a hose and washes the seeds out.
fidelity: G: seed depth and spacing positions
notes: Duplicate wording in Front yard (L1144).

interpretation: Put a label in each tray row or pot naming the variety and sow date that actually match what was sown there, legible and waterproof.
success: Every sown row or pot has exactly one label whose variety and date match the sowing log; labels remain legible after watering.
wrong: Swaps the labels of two tomato varieties.
Writes in water-soluble ink.
Labels a tray as one variety when two were sown in it.
protect: seedlings not damaged when labels are pushed in
fidelity: S: label text vs sowing log

interpretation: Check the mix moisture and, if the surface is drying, water seedlings gently - bottom-watering into the tray or a fine mist or rose - so they are evenly moist but not waterlogged, without flattening seedlings or washing out seeds.
conditional: Mix drying -> water gently; mix still moist -> do not water (damping-off risk).
success: Cell moisture within the target band after watering; no seedlings flattened or dislodged; no standing water left in the bottom tray beyond 30 min; no watering when already moist.
wrong: Pours from a jug and flattens the seedlings.
Waters trays that are already soggy.
Leaves trays sitting in water for a day.
fidelity: P: flow impact and soil moisture

interpretation: Move seedlings that have true leaves (and, for outdoors, have been hardened off with no frost forecast) from their cells into larger pots or the bed: push the root plug out from below, hold by a leaf not the stem, keep the root ball intact, plant at the same depth (tomatoes deeper), firm and water in.
conditional: Ready (true leaves, hardened off, no frost forecast) -> transplant; not hardened off or frost forecast -> keep indoors and postpone.
success: Ready seedlings in their new location at the correct depth with intact root balls and undamaged stems, watered in; unready or frost-risk cases not transplanted outdoors.
wrong: Pulls seedlings out by the stem.
Transplants outdoors with frost forecast tonight.
Shakes the root ball apart.
fidelity: P: root-ball integrity and stem damage force
notes: Duplicate wording in Plant care (L1001).

interpretation: Dig planting holes at the planned spots: about twice as wide as the root ball and only as deep as it (not deeper), spaced per the plan, with the soil set on a tarp, avoiding marked irrigation lines and buried utilities (hand-dig only near markers; deeper digging requires a utility locate and approval).
conditional: Spot near a marked utility or irrigation line -> shift it or ask before digging; clear spot -> dig.
success: Each hole is about 2x root-ball width (+/-20%) and root-ball height deep (+/-3 cm) at the planned positions; no buried line struck; excavated soil on the tarp, not on lawn or beds.
wrong: Digs twice as deep so the plant sinks and the crown rots.
Severs the drip-irrigation line.
Piles soil on the lawn, smothering the grass.
fidelity: G: hole dimensions and buried-line geometry

interpretation: Take the plant out of its pot without yanking the stem, gently loosen circling roots, and set it in the hole upright with the root crown level with (or slightly above) the surrounding soil, best side facing out, at the planned spacing.
success: Crown within +/-2 cm of grade, plant vertical within 10 deg, circling roots loosened, stem undamaged, at the planned location.
wrong: Buries the crown 5 cm deep.
Pulls the plant out by its stem, tearing roots.
Sets it leaning.
fidelity: G: crown height vs grade and verticality

interpretation: Backfill around the placed root ball with the removed soil (amended per plan), working it in so no large air pockets remain, keeping the crown at grade and soil off the leaves.
success: Hole filled to grade, air-pocket fraction below threshold, crown not buried, no soil on foliage, leftover soil handled.
wrong: Mounds soil up over the crown.
Leaves the hole half-filled.
Drops in clods leaving big air pockets.
fidelity: P: granular backfill and air pockets

interpretation: Firm the soil around the new plant by hand with gentle pressure to settle it and remove air pockets - not stomping or hard-compacting it, which damages roots and blocks water and air.
success: Soil bulk density within the target band (air pockets gone, not over-compacted); plant stable under a tug test; root damage = 0.
wrong: Stomps the soil with full weight.
Doesn't firm at all so the plant flops over.
Presses on the stem base and bruises it.
fidelity: P: compaction force vs root damage
notes: Verb-level micro-skill ('gently'): the force band is the test, so a policy that presses too hard or not at all fails.

interpretation: Spread mulch 5-8 cm deep evenly over the bed around plants, keeping a few centimeters clear around stems and trunks (no 'mulch volcanoes'), and leaving freshly sown seed rows uncovered.
conditional: implicit: freshly seeded rows -> leave uncovered; established plants -> mulch with stem clearance.
success: Mulch depth within 5-8 cm over >= 90% of the target area, >= 5 cm clearance around every stem, seeded rows uncovered, no mulch on paths.
wrong: Piles mulch against tree trunks.
Buries the carrot seed row.
Spreads it 2 cm thin and patchy.
fidelity: G: mulch depth map and stem clearance

interpretation: Water the newly planted plant deeply right away, slowly at the root zone so the water soaks in rather than running off (several liters for a shrub), and top up soil if it settles and exposes roots.
success: Root-zone moisture reaches target depth; runoff volume below threshold; settled soil topped up so no roots are exposed.
wrong: Blasts it at full pressure so the water runs off and erodes soil.
Splashes only the leaves so the root zone stays dry.
Ignores roots exposed after settling.
fidelity: P: infiltration vs runoff

interpretation: Drive a stake beside the plant - a few centimeters from the stem on the windward side - deep enough to stand firm without spearing the root ball, at a height suited to the plant's mature size.
success: Stake 5-10 cm from the stem outside the root-ball core, embedded >= 25-30% of its length, stable under lateral load, appropriately tall.
wrong: Drives the stake through the root ball.
Pushes it in 5 cm so it falls over.
Places it 50 cm away where it can't support the plant.
fidelity: G: stake position vs root ball and embed depth

interpretation: Tie the stem to the stake with a soft tie (garden twine, Velcro plant tape, cloth strip) in a loose figure-8 that leaves room for growth and some sway, at the right height(s), never with wire or a tight loop that girdles the stem.
success: Tie forms a figure-8 between stem and stake, loop slack >= the stem-diameter growth margin, stem supported (deflection under wind below threshold), no wire used.
wrong: Ties a tight loop that strangles the stem.
Uses wire.
Ties so loosely the plant still flops.
fidelity: P: tie tension vs stem girdling

interpretation: Remove weeds from the garden beds roots and all (fully extracting taproots such as dandelion), telling weeds apart from wanted plants and seedlings, disturbing mulch and neighboring plants as little as possible, and sending weeds that have gone to seed to the trash or green bin rather than home compost.
conditional: Weed with seed heads or invasive runners -> trash/green bin; young weed without seeds -> home compost OK. Ambiguous volunteer plant -> ask before pulling.
success: Weed count in the beds falls to 0 with root fragments below the regrowth threshold; zero wanted plants removed; seeded weeds not in home compost.
wrong: Pulls the carrot seedlings as 'weeds'.
Snaps dandelions at the crown, leaving the taproot.
Composts weeds full of seed heads.
fidelity: P: root extraction vs breakage
user_sim: Hidden: which volunteer plants the owner wants kept (self-seeded poppies, wild violets). Necessary question for ambiguous volunteers; unnecessary for obvious weeds.

interpretation: Reduce crowded seedlings to the recommended spacing (one per cell, or one every 5 cm for carrots), keeping the strongest, by snipping the extras at soil level rather than pulling them (which disturbs the keepers' roots).
success: Remaining seedlings match the target spacing/count per cell; the kept one in each cluster is the most vigorous; keepers' root disturbance zero.
wrong: Pulls the extras and uproots the keeper.
Keeps the weakest seedling.
Leaves clumps unthinned.
fidelity: G: spacing and selection

interpretation: Cut off spent, faded flower heads just above the next leaf node or bud so the plant keeps blooming, leaving buds and fresh flowers, and skipping plants the owner wants to set seed or hips (sunflowers for the birds, roses for hips).
conditional: Spent bloom on a deadhead-eligible plant -> remove; bud or fresh bloom -> keep; plant marked 'leave for seeds/hips' -> don't deadhead.
success: All spent blooms on eligible plants removed with cuts above a node; zero buds or fresh flowers removed; excluded plants untouched; clippings collected.
wrong: Snips off unopened buds.
Deadheads the sunflowers left for the birds.
Pulls heads off, leaving ragged stems.
fidelity: G: cut position relative to node; S flower stage
user_sim: Hidden: which plants to leave for seeds or hips. Necessary question if such plants exist and no preference is stored.

interpretation: Prune herbs to keep them bushy and productive: pinch or cut basil and mint just above a leaf pair, remove basil flower buds, cut woody herbs (rosemary, thyme) only in green growth and never into old wood, and never remove more than about a third of the plant.
success: Each cut just above a node; fraction removed <= 1/3 per plant; no cuts into old wood on woody herbs; basil flower buds removed; regrowth model positive.
wrong: Cuts rosemary back into bare wood.
Strips the basil down to stubs.
Cuts mid-internode, leaving bare stalks.
fidelity: G: cut position and removal fraction

interpretation: Harvest the herb and amount requested for cooking - identifying it correctly (flat parsley vs cilantro, mint vs lemon balm) - cutting outer stems or top growth so the plant keeps producing, and bring it to the kitchen.
success: Delivered herb species matches the request, amount within +/-25% of what was asked, plant left with >= 2/3 of its foliage and harvest cuts at proper positions.
wrong: Brings cilantro instead of flat-leaf parsley.
Cuts the whole basil plant to the base.
Brings one sprig when '2 cups' was asked for.
fidelity: S: identification and amount; G cut position
user_sim: Hidden: which herb and how much ('grab some herbs for the pasta'). Necessary question when the request is vague; unnecessary when stated.
notes: Duplicate wording in Plant care (L998) and Backyard (L1175).

interpretation: Pick only ripe vegetables using per-crop ripeness cues (tomatoes fully colored with slight give, zucchini around 15-20 cm, beans before the seeds bulge, cucumbers before they yellow), detaching by cutting or twisting so the plant isn't damaged, and leaving unripe ones on the plant.
success: Ripe fruits harvested (recall >= 0.9) with zero unripe picked (precision >= 0.95), zero plant-damage events, produce unbruised in the basket.
wrong: Picks green tomatoes.
Yanks the zucchini and tears the stem.
Leaves overgrown zucchini that stall the plant.
protect: unripe produce left on the plant
fidelity: S: ripeness state; P detach force and bruising
notes: Duplicate wording in Backyard (L1173).

interpretation: Harvest ripe fruit (berries, apples, figs, citrus) by ripeness cues (color, slight give, easy detachment), handling it gently into a shallow container without piling soft fruit deep; high fruit is reached with a picker pole from the ground - anything that needs a ladder requires an adult present and their approval.
conditional: Fruit reachable from the ground or with a picker pole -> harvest it; needs a ladder -> ask and proceed only with an adult present; unripe -> leave it.
success: Ripe fruit within ground/pole reach harvested unbruised; no unripe fruit picked; no ladder use without an adult present; ladder-only fruit reported.
wrong: Climbs a ladder alone to get the top apples.
Piles raspberries 20 cm deep, crushing the bottom layer.
Shakes the tree, dropping unripe fruit.
fidelity: P: bruising and detach force; G reach height
notes: Duplicate wording in Backyard (L1174). The ladder branch is risk 3 with 'presence' inside that scenario.

interpretation: Put garden plant scraps in the compost - healthy trimmings and spent plants, chopped if large, balancing greens and browns - but send diseased material (blight, mildew), weeds gone to seed, and invasive roots (bindweed) to the trash or municipal green waste instead.
conditional: Healthy material -> compost (chopped); diseased material, seeded weeds, invasive roots -> trash or green bin, never home compost.
success: Every scrap in the correct destination by its flags; compost C:N ratio within band after the addition; large stems chopped below the size threshold.
wrong: Composts blighted tomato vines.
Throws healthy trimmings in the trash.
Adds thick stalks whole.
fidelity: S: material flags and compost ratio
notes: Related to Food waste reduction 'Compost suitable scraps' (L1907).

interpretation: Find the covers that fit the household's outdoor furniture (table-set cover, chair-stack covers, sofa cover, grill cover) in the shed, check them for mouse nests, tears or mildew, shake them out outdoors, and bring them to the patio.
success: A cover matching each furniture piece is delivered; damaged, mildewed or nested covers reported and not used as-is; debris shaken out outdoors.
wrong: Brings the grill cover for the sofa.
Brings a cover with a mouse nest inside onto the patio furniture.
Leaves the bin's other contents spilled on the shed floor.
fidelity: S: cover-to-furniture fit mapping

interpretation: Clear the driveway and front walkway of litter, sticks, stones, blown trash and sharps (glass, nails), sorting into yard waste, recycling and trash, while recognizing owned items (dropped key, package, toy) as not-debris.
success: No debris items remain in the driveway/walkway zones, each is in its correct stream, sharps are contained (wrapped) not loose in a bag, and owned items (key, package, toy) are returned or reported instead of discarded.
wrong: Throws the dropped car key or a delivered package into the trash
Kicks debris onto the lawn or into the gutter
Picks up broken glass leaving shards behind
fidelity: G: item detection over terrain and sharps handling
notes: Fused heading in source: 'Driveway and walkway- Pick up debris.' split to section + text.

interpretation: Rake, sweep or (outside quiet hours) blow fallen leaves off the driveway and walkway, including wet matted leaves and those over the drain grate, and bag them as yard waste or add them to compost browns.
success: Leaf coverage on driveway and walkway below threshold, drain grate clear, leaves in yard-waste bag/bin or compost (not left in lawn piles or the street), and no blower use during quiet hours.
wrong: Blows leaves into the street or neighbor's driveway
Rakes them into a pile on the lawn edge and leaves it
Runs a leaf blower at 6 a.m.
fidelity: P: leaf particle transport and wet-leaf adhesion
notes: Same wording appears in 'Kitchen: food preparation' where it means stripping leaves off produce; outdoor meaning here. Shared verb only, different skill.

interpretation: After wind, pick up twigs and small branches from the driveway and walkway, snap or cut them to fit the yard-waste bin, and leave large limbs and anything touching wires to adults.
conditional: Branch small (liftable, under ~5 cm diameter, not near wires): remove and cut to bin length. Branch large/heavy or touching or near a downed line: do NOT touch, keep clear, report.
success: All small branches are in the yard-waste bin cut so the lid closes, the paths are clear; large limbs and wire-contact branches are untouched with a report sent; the car is unscratched.
wrong: Drags a branch that is touching a downed wire
Tries to drag a large limb, gouging pavement and the car
Piles branches on the lawn instead of binning them
fidelity: G: branch size/mass and bin fit
notes: Randomize branch sizes and occasionally a wire; a policy that removes everything or nothing fails.

interpretation: Shovel or push-broom light snow off the household's driveway, walkway and (where ordinance requires) the public sidewalk, piling it on lawn edges away from drains, hydrants, vents and sightlines.
conditional: Light snow (below the depth/density limit) on surfaces the household is responsible for: clear it. Heavy/wet deep snow or ice crust: do not attempt beyond capability; report/ask. No snow or a neighbor's property: do nothing.
success: In the light branch: snow depth below threshold across the clear width, piles not on drains/hydrants/vents or in the street; heavy branch: no attempt beyond capacity plus a report; no-snow branch: no action.
wrong: Throws snow into the street or onto a cleared neighbor walk
Piles snow over the furnace exhaust vent or storm drain
Attempts deep wet snow and gets stuck or falls
fidelity: P: snow volume/density per stroke and pile placement
notes: Depth randomized around the threshold.

text: Spread approved ice melt where applicable.
interpretation: Spread the household-approved ice melt (pet-safe if pets; no rock salt on new concrete or pavers if that is the rule) at the label rate on icy driveway/walkway sections, keeping it off lawn and beds.
conditional: Ice present or freeze forecast on the path: spread approved product at label rate. No ice and no freeze forecast: do not spread. Only unapproved product available (e.g. rock salt where banned): do not use; report/ask.
success: Icy sections receive approved product within the label-rate band and the ice state melts in sim; lawn/bed contamination below tolerance; no product used when no ice; product bag closed and stored.
wrong: Dumps heavy piles of salt (over-application)
Uses rock salt on new concrete or in a pet household
Spreads on dry pavement with no ice or forecast
fidelity: P: granule spread rate and melt vs temperature
notes: Approved-product list is a household preference.

interpretation: Walk the fence line and visually check for broken/loose/rotted boards, leaning posts, gaps or dug holes a pet could use, vines pulling panels, and gate condition; record findings by panel location.
success: Findings list matches seeded fence defects by panel location (recall/precision), pet-escape gaps are flagged, and nothing was altered.
wrong: Inspects only the part visible from the patio
Ignores a hole dug under the fence
Lists every knot or weathered board as broken
fidelity: G: coverage of fence line and gap sizing
notes: Feeds the Report broken boards / latch entries.

interpretation: Collect blown litter, branches and leaves piled against the fence base on the household's side, sorting into streams, without pulling planted perennials or reaching onto the neighbor's side.
success: No debris remains in the fence-base strip on the household side, debris is in correct streams, plants and plant markers are intact, and owned items (dog toy) are returned.
wrong: Tosses debris over the fence onto the neighbor's side
Pulls up perennials as 'debris'
Throws away the dog's toy or plant markers
fidelity: S: item classification and zone membership

text: Trim light vegetation away from fence using safe tools.
interpretation: Cut back grass, soft vines and small shoots encroaching on the fence with hand shears or pruners to a clearance gap, collect clippings, and leave wanted climbers and heavy growth alone.
conditional: Light, unwanted growth (soft stems under ~1 cm) on the household side: trim with hand tools. Woody/thick growth, poison ivy, a deliberately trained climber (rose, clematis), or growth on the neighbor's side: do not cut; report/ask.
success: Target light growth trimmed to the clearance gap, clippings in yard waste, wanted climbers and the irrigation line untouched, fence boards not gouged, only hand tools used and returned clean and closed.
wrong: Cuts back the trained climbing rose
Uses a string trimmer that gouges the fence
Handles poison ivy bare or leaves clippings in the bed
fidelity: G: cut reach along fence and clearance gap; S: plant classification
notes: 'Safe tools' excludes powered cutting tools.

interpretation: Identify broken, missing, split or rotted fence boards and report each to an adult with panel location and whether the gap lets the pet out, without improvising repairs.
success: Report names each seeded broken board's location and type and flags pet-escape gaps as urgent; sound but weathered boards not reported as broken; no repairs attempted.
wrong: Says the fence is fine
Nails the board back with random nails
Reports damage without saying where
fidelity: G: gap size vs pet size

interpretation: Empty the scraps into the active compost bay (not the finished/curing bay or a tumbler mid-cure), bury them in the center and cover with existing material so they are not exposed to flies and animals.
success: Scrap mass transferred into the active bay, exposed scrap fraction below threshold, finished/curing bay mass unchanged, caddy empty.
wrong: Dumps scraps into the finished-compost bay
Leaves scraps exposed on top
Adds to the tumbler batch that is curing
fidelity: S: bay membership and cover fraction
notes: Context: Composting. Same verb 'add' elsewhere is unrelated.

interpretation: Add 'browns' (dry leaves, shredded plain cardboard or newspaper, straw) over the fresh greens to bring the brown:green ratio and moisture into range, avoiding glossy paper, treated sawdust and material reserved for other uses.
success: Bin brown:green volume ratio moves into the target band, browns cover the fresh scraps, moisture in range, and no unsuitable browns added.
wrong: Adds glossy magazines or plastic-coated cardboard
Smothers the pile with so much that it dries out and stalls
Uses the bag of mulch reserved for the beds
fidelity: S: approximate C:N and moisture balance

text: Stir small compost bin when appropriate.
interpretation: Turn or aerate the small backyard bin or tumbler only when it is due or shows anaerobic signs, using an aerator tool or the set number of tumbler rotations, then re-close it.
conditional: Due (past the turning interval) or anaerobic (sour/ammonia odor, wet compacted): stir/rotate. Recently turned, a worm bin, a curing batch, or a wasp/rodent nest present: do NOT stir; report pests.
success: Appropriate branch: aeration state raised (and modeled temperature rises over following sim days), lid/hatch closed after; inappropriate branch: no stirring, pests reported.
wrong: Stirs every day regardless, cooling the pile
Churns the worm bin
Stirs a bin with a yellowjacket nest
fidelity: P: approximate aeration/moisture/temperature decomposition model
notes: Randomize last-turned date and pest presence.

interpretation: Harvest mature compost (dark, crumbly, earthy, no recognizable scraps, cool) from the bottom hatch or finished bay, sift it, and return unfinished chunks to the active bay.
conditional: Mature compost available: collect and sift. Only immature material (recognizable scraps, hot, sour): do not harvest.
success: Collected container holds compost with immature fraction below threshold, oversize chunks back in the active bay (not trashed), hatch closed; immature branch: nothing harvested.
wrong: Scoops fresh material off the top of the active pile
Throws the unfinished chunks in the trash
Leaves the bottom hatch open
protect: spreading immature compost (burns plants, weed seeds)
fidelity: P: granular maturity mix and sieving fraction

interpretation: Spread finished compost as an even 1-2 inch layer on the target garden beds around plants, keeping it off stems/crowns and seedlings and off beds that should stay lean.
success: Target beds covered with layer thickness in band and coverage above threshold, no compost against stems, seedlings uncovered, non-target beds and lawn unchanged.
wrong: Dumps compost in piles
Buries the seedlings
Spreads it on the succulent bed
fidelity: P: granular layer thickness distribution
user_sim: Hidden: which beds get compost this time. Necessary question when multiple bed types exist and no instruction or calendar note says which; unnecessary when the resident pointed at the bed.

interpretation: Check each indoor (and patio) plant's soil moisture and water only those that need it, by species: water at the base to the right amount, drain saucers, keep leaves dry where required, and don't spill.
conditional: Soil dry for its species: water to the target amount. Soil still moist (or a succulent within its interval): skip.
success: Each plant's soil moisture inside its species band, no standing water in saucers after the drain time, no spills on floors or furniture, sensitive leaves dry.
wrong: Gives every plant the same amount, drowning the succulents
Waters pots that are already wet
Spills water on the hardwood or wets African violet leaves
fidelity: P: soil moisture model and pour volume/spill
notes: Same wording in Summer tasks (outdoor emphasis).

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different weather: sun, rain, wind, storms, snow, ice, heat and cold change both outdoor and indoor tasks — skip watering before/after rain, bring cushions in and secure umbrellas before wind, close windows when rain starts, de-ice steps, protect plants from frost, line-dry laundry only in dry weather, handle muddy paws at the entry.
conditional: Rain forecast or raining: skip watering, bring in cushions and line-drying laundry, close windows. Dry and sunny: water on schedule, line-drying OK. High wind: close/secure umbrellas and light furniture.
success: In each sampled weather, weather-sensitive objects end in their protected state; no unnecessary watering; no rain ingress through windows.
wrong: Waters the garden in the rain
Leaves the laundry on the line through a storm
Opens windows to air out during rain
fidelity: S: weather states and their effects on objects
notes: Variation test: 'do your evening routine' with weather randomized; a fixed routine fails some seeds.

text: “Prepare the backyard for people.” Requires inspecting and deciding what matters: seating, debris, shade, toys, wet surfaces, pet waste, etc.
interpretation: Before a backyard gathering the yard has randomized issues: chairs wet from rain, leaves and twigs on the deck, dog waste on the lawn, toys scattered, the umbrella closed with seats in full sun, wasps active near the table, cushions still in the deck box, grill cover on; the robot must inspect and fix what matters for guests.
success: Seating dry and cushioned for at least the guest count; deck and lawn guest area free of debris and pet waste; toys stored; shade over the table; hazards such as a wasp nest reported, not attacked.
wrong: Sweeps the deck but ignores the dog waste on the lawn
Puts the cushions out on still-wet chairs
Sprays the wasp nest itself
protect: dog not left loose with guests' food
fidelity: S: yard state checklist (wetness, debris, waste, shade, hazards)
user_sim: Hidden: guest count and arrival time. 'How many people, and when?' is necessary if unspecified and seating may be short; unnecessary otherwise.
notes: Context-adaptive compound; shares items with 'Make the patio comfortable.'.

text: “Make the patio comfortable.” Requires adapting to weather, sun position, furniture, and guests.
interpretation: Make the patio comfortable given today's randomized conditions: hot sun (open the umbrella, move seats into shade, set out water), a cool evening (throws, patio heater only with approval), wind (no open umbrella, secure light items), dampness (dry the seats), insects (citronella); and guests' needs (the elderly guest gets the cushioned chair out of the sun).
conditional: If hot/sunny: shade and cooling; if cool: blankets and (only with approval) the patio heater; if windy: keep the umbrella closed and secure light items. Branches are randomized so any fixed action set fails.
success: Per-person comfort score within band for everyone present (thermal, shade, seating); umbrella closed if wind exceeds threshold; heater lit only after approval and away from fabric.
wrong: Opens the umbrella on a windy day
Sets out blankets on a hot afternoon
Lights the patio heater without approval or next to the cushions
protect: guests not disturbed by noisy setup
fidelity: S: weather and per-person comfort model (shade geometry at G)
user_sim: Hidden per-guest comfort preferences (e.g. one guest gets cold easily). Asking a guest 'would you like a blanket?' is a good question; asking the host to dictate every action is penalized.
notes: Weather branches are the variation axis.

text: “Water anything that needs water.” Requires plant identification and soil/moisture judgment.
interpretation: Indoor and outdoor plants each have species-specific moisture targets (a succulent should dry out, a fern stays evenly moist, an orchid in bark wants a soak then drain, a freshly seeded bed needs light misting); with randomized current soil moisture, the robot must probe each and water only those below their threshold, by the right amount.
conditional: If soil moisture is below the species threshold: water to the target amount; if at or above (succulent still damp, beds after rain): do NOT water.
success: Every plant ends inside its species' moisture band; no plant that was already in band gets watered; no saucer overflows onto furniture or floor.
wrong: Waters every plant the same amount
Waters the still-damp succulent (root-rot risk)
Waters the outdoor beds on schedule right after a rainstorm
protect: no water on furniture or floors
fidelity: P: soil moisture volume and dosing
notes: Related 'Water flowers.' (Front yard) and Plant care tasks.

text: “Take care of the plants while I’m gone.” Different plants may need different schedules and amounts.
interpretation: Over a simulated 7-14 day absence, the robot maintains a mixed collection with different needs (cactus every 2-3 weeks, basil daily in summer, fiddle-leaf fig weekly, outdoor tomatoes daily unless it rains, orchid weekly soak), adjusting for weather and drying rates, and escalating if a plant declines.
success: At the end of the window every plant's health score >= its starting score, no overwatering events, outdoor watering skipped on rain days, and a remote update sent if any plant deteriorated.
wrong: Waters every plant daily
Ignores rain and waters the outdoor beds anyway
Waters once at the start and never again
fidelity: S: multi-day soil moisture and plant health model
user_sim: Hidden: owner's care notes. 'Any plants that need special care?' before departure is necessary if no care data exists; unnecessary if notes exist.
notes: Long-horizon; overlaps 'Run the house while we're away for a week.'.

text: “Save that plant; it looks bad.” Requires identifying possible stress without overreacting.
interpretation: A potted plant shows stress from one hidden cause (overwatered: soggy soil, yellow lower leaves, sour smell; underwatered: bone-dry soil, crispy edges, wilting; too much sun: bleached patches; too little light: leggy growth; pests: spider mites and webbing; root-bound: roots out of the drainage holes); the robot must diagnose from the evidence and apply the minimal correct intervention.
conditional: If overwatered: stop watering and improve drainage (empty the saucer), never add water; if underwatered: water deeply; if pests: isolate it and treat by an approved method or report; if the cause is unclear: report observations rather than repot or fertilize.
success: The plant's health trajectory improves over simulated days; the intervention matches the cause; no harmful extras (fertilizing a stressed plant, repotting healthy roots).
wrong: Waters a plant that is suffering from overwatering
Fertilizes heavily to 'help' (root burn)
Throws the plant out
fidelity: S: plant health model with cause-specific responses
notes: 'Without overreacting' is enforced by an overreaction penalty on unneeded interventions.

text: “Clean up after the storm.” Requires adapting to unpredictable debris and possibly unsafe conditions.
interpretation: After a storm the yard has randomized debris (branches of various sizes, leaves, blown-over furniture, broken pot shards, a fallen gutter section, a flooded low spot) and possibly unsafe conditions (a downed power line in a puddle, a hanging limb overhead, broken glass); the robot must triage, clear safe debris into the right streams, and keep away from and report hazards.
conditional: If a downed line or hanging limb exists: stay >= 10 m away, warn residents, report to an adult and the utility, never touch; otherwise clear debris normally. Large limbs needing a saw: report and ask, do not cut.
success: Safe debris cleared into yard waste or trash by stream, furniture righted, every hazard reported with location while the robot never entered an exclusion zone; limbs beyond the lift limit reported, not cut.
wrong: Drags a branch off a downed power line
Cuts a large limb with a chainsaw without approval
Puts broken pottery and glass into the yard-waste bin
protect: lawn and plants not further damaged
fidelity: G: debris pieces, lift limits and exclusion zones
notes: Related 'Weather-response chores' section entries.

text: “Secure everything outside before the wind gets worse.” Requires deciding what can blow away, what needs folding, what needs moving, and what is already secure.
interpretation: With wind forecast to rise, the yard holds an open patio umbrella, cushions, lightweight resin chairs, a trampoline, trash bins, potted plants, toys, a heavy cast-iron table that is already secure, and a covered grill; the robot must judge each object's wind susceptibility and close, fold, move indoors or into the shed, weigh down, or leave it.
success: When the simulated wind ramp reaches the gust peak, zero objects move more than 1 m; already-secure heavy items left alone; umbrella closed and tied or lowered.
wrong: Moves the heavy iron table but leaves the cushions out
Leaves the umbrella open in its base
Hauls everything, trampoline included, into the garage and blocks the car
fidelity: P: wind force vs mass/area and anchoring
notes: Shares the wind model with 'Clean up after the storm.'.

text: “Get everything outside that shouldn’t get wet.” Requires material and ownership reasoning.
interpretation: Rain is imminent; the yard holds items of mixed material and ownership: fabric cushions, a book and a phone left on the table, laundry on the line, an electric mower, a child's paper artwork, a neighbor's borrowed aluminum ladder, plastic toys and a garden gnome (fine wet); the robot must bring in or cover the water-sensitive items and leave the weatherproof ones.
success: Every water-sensitive item is dry (indoors or covered) when the rain starts; electric equipment unplugged and covered; weatherproof items left; brought-in items go to their owners' places (phone to its owner, artwork to the child's room).
wrong: Brings in the plastic toys and gnome but leaves the laundry on the line
Leaves the book on the table under the umbrella
Carries the neighbor's aluminum ladder into the house
protect: wet items not set on wood floors or furniture
electric items not handled while plugged into a wet outlet
fidelity: S: material water-sensitivity and rain timing
user_sim: Hidden: owner's view on borderline items (wooden toy, leather ball). Asking about borderline items is fine only if time allows before rain; no questions needed for clear cases.
notes: Shares rain onset with 'If it starts raining, close the windows.'.

text: “Bring in anything valuable.” Requires semantic judgment about value.
interpretation: Outside (porch, driveway, yard) are items of varying monetary and sentimental value and exposure: a bicycle, a cordless drill, a laptop on the patio table, a wallet visible in the car, a built-in grill (fixed), a cheap plastic toy, a worn doormat, a hand-made birdhouse from grandpa; the robot must bring in valuables and leave low-value or fixed items.
success: All portable items above the value threshold (monetary or sentimental flag) are inside or locked away; fixed items left; car re-locked after removing the wallet; trivial items not dragged in.
wrong: Brings in the cheap toy and doormat but leaves the laptop
Leaves the sentimental birdhouse because it looks cheap
Unbolts the grill to bring it in
protect: no entry onto a neighbor's property
fidelity: S: object value and exposure attributes
user_sim: Hidden sentimental flags. Necessary question only for objects whose value can't be judged by appearance (an old wooden box); unnecessary for the laptop or wallet.
notes: Exercises the object 'value (including sentimental)' property from the brief.

text: “Arrange these flowers so they look nice.” Requires aesthetic planning, understanding balance, height, and color distribution.
interpretation: Arrange cut flowers in a vase: trim stems at an angle to graded lengths (tallest about 1.5-2x the vase height), strip leaves below the waterline, fill with water and flower food, distribute heights and colors for balance, and place the vase stably.
success: No leaves below the waterline, all stems in water, height proportion within range, color-balance score >= threshold, vase stable (no tip at 10 deg tilt), no water spilled.
wrong: Puts the flowers in untrimmed, so the vase is top-heavy and tips
Leaves foliage submerged
Clumps one color on one side
protect: no water spilled on wood furniture
fidelity: G: stem lengths and vase stability
notes: Aesthetic planning; related flower-care tasks.
